claim.summary: Over any field, for finite nonempty X_nu in disjoint variable blocks and X their product, with degree the least degree of a representing polynomial: the least degree of a nonzero function supported in a product set prod A_nu is sum m_nu (m_nu the least degree of a nonzero function on X_nu supported in A_nu), and degree is additive on products of block functions (union of block Groebner bases, leading monomials multiply). Hence in the degree-D vanishing ideal of X, block-local errors of degree<=e with supports Z_nu have surviving common killers of degree k (k+e<=D) exactly when k>=sum m_nu for A_nu=X_nu minus Z_nu. A separating idempotent s with s w_i = w_i and s vanishing off the union U of supports (a span generator) equals 1_U on X, so 1-s has degree sum delta(1_A_nu), which on cubes can exceed sum m_nu by the factor b (errors at block origins of {0,1}^b: m=1, delta=b); a general idempotent protecting a 0/1-valued least killer p, s=1-p, costs sum m_nu where such a p exists (always over F_2; not over F_3 on {0,1,2}); protecting one point x_0 costs sum m_nu(x_0), the blocks' least degrees of functions supported in A_nu and nonzero at x_0, which can exceed sum m_nu. Degree additivity is the standard tensor fact, proved here for finite product sets.

claim.summary: Over any field, on a finite product domain X = prod_j A_j (nonempty factors) with base states and one-hot variables x_(j,a) for non-base a (degree = least polynomial degree in them), a nonzero function vanishing on a union of cylinders (partial assignments) has degree at least the transversal number of their coordinate sets; if every coordinate of a least transversal T has a state no cylinder assigns there, the product of those state indicators (each of degree <=1) attains it. On the hole-respecting assignments of the product pigeonhole system, with base state empty, the least degree of a nonzero function vanishing on the supports of monomial errors on distinct holes is the transversal number of their hole sets, which is the least degree of a surviving common killer of 1 when tau<=K and K+e is inert, or D=n with K+e<=n and K<=n-1; for tau>K there is none of degree <=K.

significance.rationale: Gives the exact first surviving killer degree for cylinder errors on product domains, the domain-model baseline that a non-domain killer must beat.

claim.summary: Over a commutative coefficient ring, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal and w_1..w_r polynomials. If s has degree <=sigma, s w_i - w_i lies in C for every i and s p lies in C, then f=1-s kills every w_i and f p - p lies in C, so f preserves p modulo C; a sufficient case is s = sum_i a_i w_i with w_i p in C and deg a_i + deg w_i + deg p <= D, and then s^2 = s modulo C when deg a_i + sigma + deg w_i <= D. Over a field, if C is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of a finite X and k <= min(D - max deg w_i, D - deg p), a polynomial f of degree <=k kills every w_i with fp outside C exactly when f vanishes on the union Z of the w_i's supports on X and not at every point of supp(p) minus Z; the first such degree is an interpolation degree on X. On the cube 1-s is the reduced product of denominators; for pigeonhole hole factors it is the empty-column indicator.

claim.summary: Over F_p, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal containing x^2-x for every variable. If deg q<=d, P=(1-q^(p-1))R and deg h+deg P+(p-1)d<=D, then q^(p-1)Ph lies in C. So for a Pang family with t>=1 choices q_j of degree <=d, P=prod_j(1-q_j^(p-1)), Delta=(p-1)dt and errors P g_i (deg g_i<=d), every q_j^(p-1) kills every error when (p-1)d+Delta+d<=D; for S families and any choice per family, the product of these Fermat killers, of degree <=S(p-1)d, kills every error when S(p-1)d+Delta+d<=D, and in the cube's vanishing ideal survives exactly when some cube point has every chosen q nonzero. Its degree bound S(p-1)d is below Pang's multiplier degree K exactly when S<K/((p-1)d), and it is not shown to survive in Pang's proper closure.
